# M2 independent adversarial review

Final status: **the 0.2.1 repair passes independent source review, 93 unit tests, 14 core NeoForge GameTests, two real-FTB GameTests, and bounded actual-ATM10 pickaxe, persistence, reload, already-owned and warmed quest checks. No remaining blocking production issue was found in this scope.** Index coverage remains partial and quest collection sometimes times out explicitly. The original 0.2.0 failure and two hostile-mob deaths during test operation are recorded in [PLAYTEST-M2.md](PLAYTEST-M2.md). The handoff has no goal set and recovered baseline items, but the world is paused with ticks deliberately frozen and is not unchanged.

The test/verifier agent reviewed the production work independently. It wrote tests and this review, not production implementation. The review covered `knowledge/`, `planning/`, `integration/quest/`, commands, snapshot integration, mod startup, optional dependencies, persistence, and local exports.

## Actual-pack failure and verified automated repair

The original 0.2.0 artifact exhausted the shared 200,000-alternative budget before normalizing the vanilla diamond-pickaxe recipe. All five ingredient positions were explicitly unsupported. The diagnostic was truthful, but it prevented a basic material plan. The full pack contained 95,103 recipe definitions, far beyond the earlier test fixtures.

The narrow repair prioritizes inexpensive verified ingredient models before broad and opaque definitions, using recipe IDs only as a tie-breaker. Unsupported or incomplete raw expansions drop their unusable alternative lists while preserving bounded source identities. The 50,000-definition, 200,000-alternative and 400,000-identity limits remain unchanged. If a multi-input recipe runs out of budget midway, earlier known positions may remain charged; the whole recipe remains unsupported and cannot be used by the planner.

Independent source review found no new blocking correctness issue in that policy. Six additional unit regressions and a real-recipe GameTest pass, without weakening the original tests. The new runtime fixture supplies 4,000 broad recipes (256,000 potential alternatives) before the actual vanilla pickaxe, repeats with reversed input, checks the exact three-diamond/two-stick material result, and checks the original global limits. Both builds retained all 4,001 definitions, 199,941 alternatives and 399,946 identities; 876 recipes explicitly remained unsupported. Builds took 600 and 455 ms in this synthetic runtime.

The verifier independently inspected all 14 current JUnit XML reports (93 tests, zero failures/errors), the completed `m2-playtest-fix.log` (14 core and two FTB tests passed), and the real-recipe regression results. The current packaged evidence under [evidence-m2/](evidence-m2/) now corresponds to this 0.2.1 repair: [verification-final.log](evidence-m2/verification-final.log), 14 JUnit XML reports, and [m2-budget-regression.json](evidence-m2/m2-budget-regression.json). The clean combined run completed successfully in 2m 22s; core tests took 10.19 seconds and FTB tests 1.736 seconds. These automated repair results remain distinct from the actual ATM10 observations below.

The repaired artifact has initialized in actual ATM10 and built generation 1: 50,000 / 95,078 definitions, 35,338 supported material models, 200,000 retained alternatives and 400,000 identities, with 2,116 ms full build time. Coverage remains partial and the time budget is cooperative. The bare goal command confirmed AE2 goal persistence across restart. The independently inspected fresh pickaxe export proves fixed supported crafting, all five complete tag-derived requirements, and five actual wooden-rod alternatives, while the two custom routes remain unsupported previews. This verifies the original full-pack starvation regression. A real `/reload` rebuilt generation 2 (41,651 / 95,087 definitions, 35,336 supported material models, 200,000 alternatives, 397,086 identities, 2,634 ms), again with partial coverage. A fresh post-reload recipe export preserves the same pickaxe requirements. A fresh 1,821-byte plan proves `already_owned` for one restored plush using generation 2, with no missing materials or steps, zero nodes/depth and 1.1476 ms planner time. Quest context in that plan is explicitly unavailable after the 250 ms budget, not empty or known. A subsequent independent log check confirms warmed quest success: nine completed, 4,555 available incomplete and 226 blocked. Timeouts remain part of the result.

## Operational handoff

The verifier independently confirmed log messages for two Tombstone inventory recoveries, a cleared/no-current goal, normal tick resumption, and subsequent tick freezing. Root observed two hostile-mob deaths while operating the live test, the second before an intended pause took effect. Both graves were recovered through the installed mod's supported transfer/cleanup command. Root's final visual check confirmed the original plush and guide book plus additional flower/dirt stacks, full health/hunger and XP 0; extra pickups' cause was not verified. No claim is made that inventory, position, death history, advancements or quest progress are unchanged.

The actual world is finally **paused with server ticks deliberately frozen** to avoid another incident. The user must run `/tick unfreeze` when ready to resume safely. No Companion goal remains. This operational state and the remaining world changes are disclosed; they do not change the production test results or imply that the world was rolled back. No further game input is planned.

## Findings corrected before sign-off

1. **Dropped recipe definitions could look like complete knowledge.** An index with one inspected definition and zero retained definitions could previously return `complete=true`. Completeness now requires inspected and indexed counts to agree, no truncation or unknown outputs, and fixed outputs for every retained recipe. A regression test constructs the omitted-definition case directly.
2. **Opaque prerequisites were hidden behind resource acquisition advice.** A plan requiring an unsupported machine component and four diamonds previously suggested obtaining diamonds first. The next action now prioritizes inspecting the unsupported prerequisite. The known diamond shortage remains a separate fact.
3. **Optional-adapter test code did not compile.** An overloaded `ArrayList.add` method reference was ambiguous between one-argument and two-argument diagnostic callbacks. Explicit one-argument lambdas fix the tests; production callback behavior was unchanged.
4. **Two initial runtime fixtures were invalid.** Posting a player-join sync with a FakePlayer reached unrelated NeoForge networking without a channel; the fixture now uses the official embedded-connection mock ServerPlayer. The malformed SavedData fixture assumed its player occupied the first entry, but another concurrent fixture could add entries. It now corrupts the explicit target UUID and requires that target to be rejected while the other player's goal remains unchanged. These corrections preserve the production assertions. The initial core run passed 11/13 tests; the corrected run passed 13/13.
5. **The FTB fixture initially lacked a valid modded test connection.** FTB's progress-update payload was rejected; configuring mock negotiation after login was too late once an existing quest book sent login payloads. The fixture now creates an ordinary ServerPlayer and embedded connection, invokes NeoForge's official `NetworkRegistry.configureMockConnection` before login, and leaves production packet checks intact. A subsequent test profile had 17 characters, exceeding Minecraft's 16-character packet limit. A valid fixture name and an exact test-only repair of that fixture's persisted invalid name resolved the problem. Real FTB models, progression predicates, and team assertions were not replaced or weakened.

The implementation agents also strengthened recipe identity/global retention bounds and preserved conservative chapter visibility in derived quest availability. Independent regression tests cover those boundaries.

## Source review conclusions

- Runtime registries, recipe definitions, ingredient item/tag values, inventory stacks, and FTB APIs supply gameplay facts. No ATM10 recipe ingredients or quest completion values are hardcoded.
- Recipe DTOs detach from live Minecraft objects. Exact verified vanilla crafting/cooking classes may support material dependencies; custom predicates, dynamic previews, component outputs, empty tags, fluids, and unmodeled machine conditions remain unsupported. Empty tags never become NeoForge barrier display placeholders.
- The immutable recipe index has explicit per-output route retention and global bounds. Unsupported previews do not displace all supported routes. Startup/reload replaces the cache; an unsuccessful rebuild removes stale usable facts. Queries enforce the server thread.
- Planner ledgers distinguish original inventory, missing resources, and hypothetical batch surplus. Original stacks are shared across all sibling requirements. Missing materials do not become owned items. Cycles, unknown processing, and search limits produce explicit issues. Recipes are suggested in prerequisite order, and material readiness is not execution readiness.
- Optional FTB classes are behind a release gate and lazy factory. Missing/incompatible/failed integration is distinct from an observed empty quest file. Progress belongs to the invoking player's current FTB team; observation does not create team progression. Dependency operators and exact task matching remain unavailable when not exported.
- Derived available quests require observed chapter visibility, quest visibility, unlocked team, FTB task-start permission, and incomplete status. Raw observed flags remain separate. Quest-ID ordering is deterministic, not strategic ranking.
- Graph ingredient alternatives are explicitly OR choices. Capped graph projection marks truncation and omits edges whose endpoints cannot be retained.
- Goals use bounded world SavedData keyed by player. Exports use fixed server-local filenames, operator permission, size-bounded JSON, and replacement writes. No client-only class references, AI service, networking client, credentials, server-address export, background world reads, or automatic transmission were found in production sources.

The real fixture proves partial task progress 2/3, completion at 3/3, dependency unlocking, `one_completed` semantics without inventing an AND rule, team locking, current-party resolution, missing-team noncreation, and explicit unknown task matching. The retained quest JSON has schema 1, the supported source version, and `current_player_ftb_team` scope. Core startup retained 1,294 definitions across 842 output items in 95 ms; the two reload builds took 48/60 ms. The optional runtime retained 1,298 definitions across 846 output items in 109 ms. These are small test-environment measurements, not full-pack performance estimates.

## Accepted limitations

The planner is a bounded material search, not a complete planner, action executor, or strategic ranker. It can miss better routes or allocations. It does not credit containers or byproducts, prove access to processing devices/fuel/power, inspect external storage, or infer specialized machine/fluid semantics. Unknown or truncated index coverage cannot establish that no recipe exists.

Extraction time budgets are cooperative: they bound work between API calls and cannot preempt a third-party API call that hangs. Export size limits can reject a large report rather than silently publish an incomplete report as complete. The snapshot JSON reader is a debug/test codec, not an exposed importer or exhaustive hostile-input schema validator.
